desc: Prove impossibility cases: parity argument — red's outgoing move flips (r+c) parity, blue's preserves it, so R must be even; if R=0, diagonal-move graph is bipartite (r-parity flips each move), so B must be even. Feasible iff R even and (R>0 or B even).
Design construction for B=0, R even (R=2: adjacent pair (1,1),(1,2); R>=4: perimeter of 2 x (R/2) rectangle).
Design construction for R=0, B even (B=2: (1,1),(2,2); B=2k>=4: diamond/stadium loop (2,2),(3,3),...,(k+1,k+1),(k+2,k),(k+1,k-1),...,(3,1)).

Design construction for mixed case (R even >=2, any B>=1): unified construction — red path from v_0=(2,2) via column-1/2 "teeth" to v_{R-1} ((1,2) for odd B, (1,4) for even B with R>=4, (2,3) for even B with R=2), then blue diamond path from b_1 ((1,3) odd / (2,4) even) down-right, down-left, up-left to b_B=(3,3), closing diagonally to v_0. Verified on samples and multiple small cases by hand.
Implement solver reading T cases, applying feasibility check and constructions, outputting placements.

Independently verify the solver: brute-force checker validating all constructions for small (R,B) (distinct cells, move types, cyclic closure) plus exhaustive search for small R+B to confirm feasibility characterization; no discrepancies found.
